instructions: You'll need a khanom krok pan. A takoyaki pan or a paniyaram pan works too.
Make the batter. In a bowl, whisk 1 cup of the rice flour, the glutinous rice flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Stir in 3/4 cup of the coconut milk. Boil 1 cup water, pour it in and whisk until smooth.
Make the filling. In another bowl, stir the remaining 3/4 cup coconut milk with the remaining 1 tbsp rice flour, the sugar and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the scallions thin. Thaw the corn and drain it.
Heat the pan over medium heat. Flick a few drops of water on it. They should sizzle. Brush each mold well with oil.
Stir the batter and fill each mold about 3/4 full. Swirl the pan or use a spoon so the batter coats the sides of each mold up to the rim.
Stir the filling and spoon 1 to 2 tsp into each mold. Cover the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Uncover and add a few corn kernels and a pinch of scallion to each. Cover again and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the top is no longer sticky when you touch it lightly.
Run a spoon around the sides to loosen each pancake and lift it out. Stir the batter and the filling before each batch. Serve hot, right away.
If you'd like to get ahead, make the batter and the filling the day before and keep them covered in the fridge.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings that could be read (Hot Thai Kitchen and Inquiring Chef were blocked), so the lead is Rak's Kitchen (5 from 3 votes). Hungry in Thailand agrees on the two batters, a rice flour shell and a coconut milk filling, cooked covered in a molded pan; it uses more batter, palm sugar in the shell and no corn. The pancakes are not good for freezing. The corn and scallion amounts are not given by the lead, so they are a small topping.
